title: In 197 Zambian fruit-fly genomes, half of the constrained non-coding DNA lies outside 1,345 open-chromatin maps, mostly as conserved sequence within 1 kb of the peaks
abstract:
In the fruit fly, half of the non-coding DNA that natural selection keeps unchanged is outside every open-chromatin peak in 1,345 public experiments; most of it is conserved sequence within 1 kb of a peak. This matters because open-chromatin maps are the main guide to functional non-coding DNA, and here conservation finds the selected DNA much better than the maps do.

We used 197 Drosophila melanogaster genomes from Zambia (DPGP3), D. simulans as outgroup, and all public fly ATAC-seq and DNase-seq experiments in ChIP-Atlas. These assays find open chromatin, that is, DNA without nucleosomes, where most known enhancers are. Constraint is the fraction of new mutations that selection removes, measured from divergence (C_D) or from diversity in the 197 genomes (C_pi), relative to neutral short-intron sites with base composition and 1-Mb windows matched. On the autosomes, 55% of non-repeat intron and intergenic DNA (29.1 Mb) was never open. Its constraint was C_D 0.53 (95% CI 0.52-0.55) and C_pi 0.48 (0.45-0.50), against 0.66 and 0.62 for non-coding DNA open at least once, so it holds 50% of the constrained non-coding sites. DNA with no peak in 6,277 open-chromatin, histone, RNA polymerase II and transcription-factor experiments still had C_D 0.48. Of the selected never-open sites, 84-87% are in phastCons-conserved elements (conserved by alignment of 27 insects): conserved never-open DNA had C_pi 0.71, close to 0.76 for conserved open DNA, and non-conserved never-open DNA had only 0.17. 90% of never-open DNA is within 1 kb of a peak, and its constraint changes little with distance to the peak. Adding the experiments in random order lowered the constraint of the DNA not yet open only from 0.59 to 0.53, without saturation; DNA open only in 28 pupal experiments had C_D 0.80. Rare alleles were in excess in all four mutation types; this is clean evidence of selection only for the conserved never-open DNA. At least about 60% of new mutations in never-open DNA have a scaled selection coefficient 4Ns below -1; the share below -100 is not identified, because the model fit depends on an unknown mutation-rate ratio or on a non-selective distortion of the allele-frequency spectrum. SNPs that create strong motif matches in dark DNA were not rarer than other SNPs.

Limits: values are relative to short introns; peaks are uniformly called but most samples are embryos, larvae and brains; an independent review removed an earlier claim of weak selection.

display.caption: Constraint (1 - divergence / neutral divergence) of D. melanogaster autosomal non-coding DNA by the number of ATAC-seq or DNase-seq experiments (of 1,345) with a peak over the site. Never-open DNA (0) has constraint 0.53; fully dark DNA (no peak of any kind in 6,277 experiments) has 0.48. Dashed lines: coding and UTR classes. Error bars: 95% CI, 1-Mb block bootstrap.

Conservation, not openness, marks the selected non-coding DNA. Left and middle: divergence-based and diversity-based constraint for never-open and open non-coding DNA, inside and outside phastCons 27-way elements (divergence values for conserved DNA are partly circular; diversity values are not). Right: diversity-based constraint of never-open DNA by distance to the nearest ATAC/DNase peak; 90% of never-open DNA is within 1 kb of a peak. Error bars: 95% CI, 1-Mb block bootstrap.

Saturation analysis. Experiments are added in 20 random orders. Left: share of non-coding DNA not yet open. Middle: constraint of that residual. Right: share of all constrained non-coding sites inside the residual. After 1,345 experiments the residual is 55% of non-coding DNA, has constraint 0.53, and holds 50% of the constrained sites.
